results.summary: This project is a hardware EEPROM wear-leveling controller implementing the Start-Gap algorithm with a 2-round Feistel address scrambler. It maintains an 8-entry logical-to-physical mapping table and 16-bit wear counters per physical block, triggering remaps when wear differences exceed a threshold. Additional features include Hamming(6,3) single-error correction, bad-block retirement, saturating wear counters, and an in-band telemetry port. The purely digital finite-state machine is written in Verilog and verified with a Cocotb testbench.

results.summary: This project is an enable-controlled 8-bit sigma-delta decimator ADC for 1-bit bitstreams. The incoming bitstream is sampled by the Tiny Tapeout clock and a 256-cycle decimator counts ones to produce a raw 8-bit code. Gain trim and signed offset trim are applied, with the calibrated result output on uo[7:0] and status bits {saturated, activity, busy, valid} on uio[7:4]. It is written in Verilog and verified with a cocotb testbench.

results.summary: This project is a PWM generator with configurable period and duty cycle via 8-bit input pins. It uses a two-process finite-state machine structure consisting of an 8-bit counter and an 8-bit comparator, with the period set on ui_in and the duty cycle set on uio_in. The module continuously increments the counter and compares it against the duty cycle configuration to drive uo_out[0] HIGH or LOW, with asynchronous reset and synchronous enable. An LED or PMOD LED module can be connected to uo_out[0] to observe brightness scaling with duty cycle.
